<reason>Side A wins by holding PRO to the proposition as written. B effectively distinguishes confidential pooling from public information, but its answers concede common use alone is insufficient and require pooling, adherence, and discipline—facts A accepts would prove actual coordination. A also undercuts the asserted rim by showing visibility and losing tenants are competition, not agreement or retaliation, while exposing the burden-shifting cost of cartel-level scrutiny.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Most decisive was A's Rebuttal 2: answering that proven pooling-plus-commitment would warrant scrutiny, then showing B's narrowed test is A's evidence-first standard rather than category-wide treatment as direct coordinators.</best_rebuttal>
